concerns.text: T001 is tagged [P] and sequenced alongside T002, but its own verification is a consumer of later tasks' outputs: 'python code/main.py --mode synthetic --n-subjects 100 --seed 42 completes without error' and run_quickstart_test.py 'assert[s] exit 0 and schema-valid outputs' require the generator (T002), preprocessing (T003), and connectivity (T004) to exist and produce schema-valid artifacts. As written, T001 cannot pass its verification before T004, so the [P] tag is unsafe and the stated execution order 'T001 → T002 → ...' contradicts T001's acceptance criteria. Either scope T001's verification to entry-point/argparse-level checks only (e.g. --help exit 0, flags parsed, real_ingest stub exits 0), or move the end-to-end quickstart assertion to the Phase-1 checkpoint / a later task.

T001's run_quickstart_test.py 'subprocess-invoke[s] the exact quickstart commands' — the quickstart commands include the synthetic generator invocation, creating a hidden ordering dependency between the two [P]-tagged tasks T001 and T002. State explicitly that the quickstart smoke test is only runnable at/after the Phase-1 checkpoint, or defer its full assertion there.
